1.explanation: The root of the problem is the regular expression that defines how Prism recognizes string literals in the basic language definition (which VB.NET extends). In both prism-basic.js and its minified version, the pattern for the 'string' token only allows a specific set of characters inside quotes—'@' is not included. As a result, when an '@' appears, the regex fails to match the opening quote and the rest of the text is not treated as part of the string. To fix this, '@' must be added to the allowed character class in the 'string.pattern' regex.
1.bug_scenario: In VB.NET code, when a string literal contains an '@' character (for example, "Select * from test Where Code=@Code"), Prism’s VB.NET syntax highlighter fails to recognize the opening quote and highlights the remainder of the line as code rather than as a string. Strings without '@' work correctly.

2.explanation: The root of the bug is in the definition of the ‘string’ token in the basic language (components/prism-basic.js and its minified counterpart). The regex character class for matching the contents of a quoted string does not include the '@' symbol, so strings containing '@' are cut off at that point. Since prism-vbnet.js simply extends Prism.languages.basic without overriding the string pattern, VB.NET inherits the same faulty regex. To fix the issue, update the character class in the ‘string’ pattern to include '@', ensuring that any string literal containing '@' is recognized and highlighted correctly.
2.bug_scenario: In VB.NET code samples containing SQL strings with an '@' parameter (e.g. "Select * from test Where Code=@Code"), Prism’s syntax highlighter fails to recognize the opening quote as part of a valid string literal once it hits the '@' character. As a result the rest of the line is highlighted as code rather than as part of the string. The second example without '@' highlights correctly.
